outcome: maternal outcomes (postpartum hemorrhage, preterm premature rupture of membranes, pre-eclampsia, maternal deaths)
fetal outcomes (foetal growth restriction, fetal deaths, live births, APGAR scores, low birth weight)
cohort: The study included nine pregnant women aged 21-31 years, mostly multigravida, presenting to a tertiary healthcare facility in Chennai with beta thalassemia trait, hemoglobinopathy E, or sickle cell trait.
finding: Early and accurate diagnosis of hemoglobinopathies in pregnancy, coupled with tailored interventions, was associated with generally favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes, with no reported instances of pre-eclampsia, fetal growth restriction, or maternal/fetal deaths.
birth_weight: Two cases were born with low birth weight.
gest_age: Gestational age at diagnosis ranged from 17-35 weeks; most deliveries occurred at term.
